standard_prerequisites: The projective bundle formula and the associated canonical surjection onto the tautological quotient with its finite locally free kernel of rank one less
Injectivity of pullback along the projection of a projective bundle, for every base change
Filtrations of locally free sheaves with invertible successive quotients, and flat projective morphisms of a given relative dimension
core_obligations: Prove the statement by induction on the total rank of the given collection
Settle the base cases: if the total rank is zero or all the sheaves have rank one, the identity morphism works
Otherwise choose a sheaf of rank greater than one, form its projective bundle, and use that the canonical map onto the tautological quotient is surjective with locally free kernel of rank one less
Observe that the projection is injective on Chow groups after every base change by the projective bundle formula, so it suffices to prove the statement upstairs
Replace the chosen sheaf by its kernel, which reduces the total rank by one, and conclude by the induction hypothesis
proof_roadmap: Induct on the total rank and dispose of the trivial cases
Pass to the projective bundle of a sheaf of larger rank, recording injectivity of the projection and the locally free kernel
Replace that sheaf by its kernel and apply the induction hypothesis
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the splitting principle at source lines 5003-5017, label lemma-splitting-principle, whose proof occupies source lines 5019-5040. The proof is an induction on the total rank which simultaneously produces the covering morphism and keeps track of the two properties demanded of it. The key step passes to the projective bundle of a sheaf of rank greater than one, uses that the canonical surjection onto the tautological quotient has a locally free kernel of rank one less, and replaces the sheaf by that kernel so that the total rank drops by one; injectivity of pullback along the projection is supplied by the projective bundle formula for every base change, which is what allows the statement to be checked upstairs. The counted statement records neither the induction nor the substitution by the kernel.
